header: The engine of the full calculator (basic and scientific, laid out like the Mac's). It is a pure state machine: `press(state, key)` gives the next state. No screen, no storage, nothing sent anywhere; the memory (mc, m+, m-, mr) and the history live only in the state of the window. How it behaves, as the Mac's does: BASIC immediate execution: 2 + 3 × 4 = 20 (each operator finishes the one before it). SCIENTIFIC the usual precedence: 2 + 3 × 4 = 14, with brackets, powers, roots and the functions; "2nd" swaps the inverse and alternate functions. "=" pressed again repeats the last operation (2 + 3 = = gives 8); "%" is the pocket-calculator percent (200 + 10 % = 220); trig works in degrees or radians (Rad / Deg); EE enters an exponent (1.5 EE 3 = 1500); a function (sin, √, x²…) acts on the number shown at once. I clean answers to 12 significant digits, so that 0.1 + 0.2 shows 0.3 and sin 180° shows 0. Number base (scientific only): DEC, BIN, OCT or HEX. In BIN, OCT and HEX the entry is the digits of the number in that base ("FF", "-1010"), whole numbers only: I make a result with a fraction an error ("Whole numbers only"), never rounded, and so is one beyond 2^53 - 1, which a float cannot hold exactly ("Too large for this base"). `enabled(state, key)` says which keys mean something in the base (a digit the base does not have, and the keys that make fractions, do not); the calculator greys the others and the engine ignores them, from this one list. The working numbers (the stack, the memory) are plain values, so a change of base only changes how they are written.

doc: The number base changed: the entry is the same value written in the new base. Only the scientific calculator has bases. behaviours: basic: immediate execution, 2 + 3 × 4 = 20
basic: a chain shows each running total: 2 + 3 + shows 5
an operator pressed twice is changed, not added: 5 + × 3 = 15
'=' again repeats the last operation: 2 + 3 = = is 8, 10 × 2 = = = is 80
'2 + =' uses the number shown twice: 4
decimals are cleaned: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3; 1 ÷ 3 shows 12 digits
a typed number grows, a second dot is ignored, a leading dot gives 0.
the sign key: 5 ± is -5, ± again is 5; zero stays zero
the percent of the pocket calculator: 200 + 10 % = 220, 200 × 10 % = 20, 50 % = 0.5, 200 - 10 % = 180
backspace deletes the last digit, down to 0; it does nothing to a result
C clears the number being typed, AC clears everything (the memory stays)
division by zero is an error that the next digit clears: 5 ÷ 0 =
memory: m+ adds, m- takes away, mr recalls, mc clears
x², x³, √, ∛, 1/x act on the number shown at once
√ of a negative number and 1/0 are errors; ∛ of a negative number is not
x!: 5! = 120, 0! = 1; a fraction or a negative number is an error
sin, cos, tan in degrees: sin 30 = 0.5, cos 60 = 0.5, tan 45 = 1, sin 180 = 0, cos 90 = 0; tan 90 is an error
in radians: sin of π/2 is 1; the angle key switches both ways
the inverse trig functions answer in the angle unit: asin 0.5 = 30°, acos 0.5 = 60°, atan 1 = 45°; asin 2 is an error
hyperbolic and inverse hyperbolic: sinh 0 = 0, cosh 0 = 1, tanh 0 = 0, asinh 0 = 0, acosh 1 = 0; acosh 0.5 is an error
logs and powers: ln e = 1, log 1000 = 3, log₂ 8 = 3, e^0 = 1, 10^3 = 1000, 2^10 = 1024; ln 0 is an error
brackets nest and close by themselves at '=': 2 × (3 + (4 × 5)) = 46; 2 × (3 + 4 = 14
a closing bracket with none open does nothing; brackets are for the scientific mode only
a result of a bracket takes part in what follows: (1 + 2) × 3 + 4 = 13
EE: 1.5 EE 3 = 1500; 2 EE 3 × 2 = 4000; EE with nothing typed means 1e
Rand gives the number it is handed
huge and tiny results go to an exponent: 10 ^ 20 and 1 ÷ 10 ^ 10
digits stop at 15
the pending work is shown: 2 + ( 3 ×
numbers are shown in Indian grouping: 12,34,567.5; 999; -1,00,000; an exponent as it is
the history keeps what was calculated, newest last, 30 at most, and holds no more than text
changing the mode drops the pending work but keeps the number and the memory
2nd only toggles; the keys it chooses between are the screen's business
a very long chain stays correct: 1 + 2 + … + 100 = 5050
the keyboard: digits, signs, Enter, Backspace, Delete, and no key at all for a Ctrl or Cmd shortcut or a letter that is not ours
a result from the history can be put back
